steps.blockerTip: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS unless using localhost, according to secondary guides.
steps.detail: Go to the Airtable Developer hub, OAuth integrations, and click Register an OAuth integration. Add a name and your exact redirect URL.
steps.title: Register an OAuth integration

steps.blockerTip: Client secret is shown only once. Store it securely at generation time.
steps.detail: Note the Client ID, then generate the client secret and store it securely, never in client code or a public repo.
steps.title: Save the Client ID and Client Secret

steps.blockerTip: Records, comments, schema, webhooks, and user email are separate scopes. Request only what the feature uses.
steps.detail: Select scopes for your feature, for example data.records:read and data.records:write for records, schema.bases:read for base structure, and user.email:read for user identity. Add webhook:manage only if webhooks are needed.
steps.title: Choose minimum scopes

steps.blockerTip: Authorize endpoint is airtable.com/oauth2/v1/authorize and token endpoint is airtable.com/oauth2/v1/token, according to secondary guides. Confirm both on official docs before shipping.
steps.detail: Redirect the user to the authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, scope, and state. Exchange the returned code for an access token at the token endpoint, then call the API with that token.
steps.title: Build the authorization flow

steps.blockerTip: If consent shows extra scopes, fix the authorize URL and scope checkboxes, not just the app settings alone.
steps.detail: Authorize with a test account, confirm the consent screen shows only the scopes you requested, and confirm a token works for one real API call, for example reading a record.
steps.title: Test with your own account

guides.tested: Docs research on 2026-10-31 from Nango, Formbricks, and Pipedream scope lists, plus Airtable developer pages.
